QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Landscape and Types_7

question.text: Under Section 2(h) of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 as summarised in the chapter, which of the following is NOT included within the definition of 'securities'?

answer.text: Units or instruments issued by a pooled investment vehicle
A unit-linked insurance policy providing combined life-risk and investment benefit

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The chapter reproduces Section 2(h) SCRA 1956 with explicit carve-out for insurance-linked units: 'securities do not include any unit linked insurance policy or scrips or any such instrument or unit, by whatever name called which provides a combined benefit risk on the life of the persons and investment by such persons and issued by an insurer'. Hence ULIPs are NOT 'securities' under SCRA. The other three (pooled investment vehicle units, derivatives, government securities) are explicitly included. **The Trap:** (A), (B) and (D) are all listed in Section 2(h). The exception clause for ULIPs is easy to miss because ULIPs are sold like mutual funds. Remember the carve-out is specifically for ULIPs issued by INSURERS under the Insurance Act. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A / III-B (Compliance Officers) test SCRA definitions in depth. XIX-A and XXI-A (Distributor exams) test it for product scope. XIX-C also covers it. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For Cat I/II Managers structuring a fund, this distinction matters when choosing the pooling vehicle — an AIF unit is a 'security'; a ULIP is not. Cross-holdings in ULIPs by an AIF scheme are not permissible AIF investments under the investment-policy section of the PPM.
